title: Relatively flat modules have no sections supported over a Cartier divisor
statement:
Let $g:Y\to T$ be any morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Let $D\subseteq T$ be an effective Cartier divisor, meaning a closed subscheme with quasi-coherent ideal locally generated by a non-zero-divisor [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal], [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $\mathcal M$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-module [pqf-def-coherent] flat over $T$ through $g$ [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. Then $\mathcal M$ has no nonzero local sections supported on $g^{-1}|D|$: for every open $W\subseteq Y$ the restriction
$$\mathcal M(W)\longrightarrow\mathcal M(W\setminus g^{-1}|D|)$$
is injective. More precisely, for every affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq T$ on which $D$ is cut out by a non-zero-divisor $a\in A$, and every affine open $W\subseteq g^{-1}V$, multiplication by the image of $a^n$ is injective on $\mathcal M(W)$ for every $n\geq0$; a section restricting to zero on the principal open of $W$ defined by the image of $a$ is therefore zero.

proof.text: Fix affine opens $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq T$ and $W=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq g^{-1}V$ as in the statement, with Cartier equation $a\in A$. Put $N=\mathcal M(W)$ and let $b\in B$ be the image of $a$. By [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over], $N$ is flat over $A$. The non-zero-divisor condition says that the $A$-linear map $\mu_a:A\to A$, $r\mapsto ar$, is injective. The complement of $g^{-1}|D|$ in $W$ is $D(b)$: a point is outside the inverse image exactly when its prime ideal does not contain $b$.

source.place: Tag 01U4, lemma-flat-module-characterize (1) iff (2); local Cartier equation

proof.text: Apply the existing Mathlib corollary Module.Flat.isSMulRegular_of_nonZeroDivisors of tensor preservation of injections [lem-trf-flat-tensor-preserves-injection] to the flat A-module N and the non-zero-divisor a^n (pow_mem ha n), for each n, including n=0. Its proof tensors the injective multiplication map and uses the tensor-unit identification. Under the Module.compHom scalar structure from g.appLE, this scalar action is multiplication by the image of a^n; map_pow identifies it with b^n. This gives the power injectivity without repeating the tensor-unit calculation or an induction in this module.

If $s\in\mathcal M(W)$ restricts to zero on $D(b)$, clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-module-basic-open-localization] supplies $n\geq0$ such that $b^n s=0$. The hypotheses are precisely that $W$ is affine and $\mathcal M$ is quasi-coherent; no flatness of $B$ over $A$ is required. The injectivity just proved gives $s=0$. This proves the principal-open assertion as well as the claimed injectivity of every power.

source.place: Tag 07ZP, lemma-sections-supported-on-closed-subset (2), principal-ideal case; also the cited affine localization lemma

proof.text: Now let $H\subseteq Y$ be any open and $s\in\mathcal M(H)$ restrict to zero on $H\setminus g^{-1}|D|$. The Cartier condition provides an affine open cover $V_i$ of $T$ with non-zero-divisor equations $a_i$. Cover each $H\cap g^{-1}V_i$ by affine opens $W_{ij}$. Each $s|_{W_{ij}}$ vanishes on the principal complement and hence is zero by the preceding step. Since the $W_{ij}$ cover $H$, the uniqueness axiom of the sheaf $\mathcal M$ gives $s=0$. Applying this to the difference of two sections proves the asserted injectivity on $H$.

lean.statement: theorem relative_flat_cartier_support {Y T : Scheme.{u}} (g : Y ⟶ T) (D : T.IdealSheafData) (hD : D.IsInvertible) (M : Y.Modules) [SheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherent (R := Y.ringCatSheaf) M] (hflat : M.IsFlatOver g) : (∀ H : Y.Opens, Function.Injective (M.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left : H ⊓ g ⁻¹ᵁ D.support.compl ≤ H)).op)) ∧ (∀ (V : T.affineOpens) (W : Y.affineOpens) (e : W.1 ≤ g ⁻¹ᵁ V.1) (a : Γ(T, V.1)), a ∈ nonZeroDivisors Γ(T, V.1) → D.ideal V = Ideal.span {a} → (∀ n : ℕ, Function.Injective (fun s : Γ(M, W.1) ↦ (g.appLE V.1 W.1 e a) ^ n • s)) ∧ (∀ s : Γ(M, W.1), M.presheaf.map (homOfLE (Y.basicOpen_le (g.appLE V.1 W.1 e a))).op s = 0 → s = 0))
